checkpoint: final adapter of the fixed schedule only; no intermediate checkpoint is ever evaluated on the gate

descriptive_slices.input_kind: upstream test call versus novel perturbation
descriptive_slices.status: DESCRIPTIVE, likely underpowered; never cross-dataset generalisation

estimand: COMPOSITE objective intervention: value_only versus full_completion changes WHICH completion tokens are supervised, HOW MANY target tokens are supervised, their POSITIONS, and the RELATIVE per-example and per-token weighting of the loss (the loss averages over supervised tokens, so each value token's share changes); it is not a scalar gradient-dose reduction and does not isolate value-token location

guardrails.answer_rate: T - C answer rate >= -2.0 points, per schema
guardrails.reference_validity: T - C mean per-requested-candidate reference validity >= -3.0 points
guardrails.status: POINT-ESTIMATE OPERATIONAL SAFETY THRESHOLDS; paired cluster-bootstrap intervals reported alongside

looks: exactly one gate look per arm; the analysis refuses to run twice

outcomes.inconclusive_power: anything else; never 'no effect', never rejects
outcomes.operational_guardrail_stop: otherwise, any guardrail point estimate beyond its threshold (not a statistical claim of harm)
outcomes.promising: otherwise, primary lower bound > 0 under both schemas with no sign flip
outcomes.statistically_supported_adverse: a primary upper bound < 0 under either schema, or a guardrail's upper bound below its threshold

power_at_gate.reading: a five-point true effect has low useful detection power at 200 groups; detection is not impossible

primary.keys: every gate group x {upstream, novel} x both schemas, exactly once
primary.metric: fixed-input exact-output accuracy (assert CALL == ANSWER passes on the reference)

reported_metrics: function-level P(at least one valid killing candidate)

why: v1 did not require exact key sets or list every metric
